verdict: No overall latency/reliability improvement demonstrated for the current sequential JEV implementation.
scope: Same two public English/Korean queries, three candidates each, five repetitions per language and arm; local ranking only, not deployed end-to-end search.
interpretation: JEV's sample median was lower than cold standard, but its successful-attempt mean was about 26% higher and two queries timed out. Warm standard benefits from HyDE and embedding caches that the current JEV evaluator does not have.
limitations: With ten attempts, nearest-rank p95 equals the maximum; not a reliable production percentile.
Cold standard control was measured after the interleaved first pilot, so conditions are not perfectly simultaneous.
HTTP timeout was 10 seconds with no retries, and query deadline was 25 seconds; baseline uses isolated caches rather than deployed server state.
Three candidates and two simple synthetic-labeled queries do not establish representative workload performance or quality parity.
Measured existing JEV sequential per-candidate requests only; no claims about batched or concurrent JEV.
No production search behavior was changed.
